title: Dashboarding for Q1 2026 perf baseline runs (drilldowns to manifests + traces)
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Goal
Build baseline dashboards for the Q1 2026 perf baseline & representative workload suite with drill-down links from a high-level view (exec/runtime/SRE friendly) to the exact run manifest + primary trace artifacts.

This ticket covers:
- Dashboards for baseline reporting (TTFT/TPOT percentiles, throughput) + variance/saturation panels
- Templated filtering by model family, model id, region, GPU SKU, runtime build, scheduler config, workload suite version, cache scenario (cold/warm), and run_id
- Drill-down links: dashboard panel -> run manifest (JSON) -> trace/pyroscope/flamegraph (where available) -> kernel selection dump (where enabled)
- Role-based views: Runtime engineering vs SRE/on-call

Out of scope
- Defining regression thresholds (ENG-4828)
- Defining canonical run manifest schema (ENG-4822 / ADR-0172)
- Reworking metric emission names in runtime beyond what’s required for dashboard joinability (should be handled by ENG-4826 / metrics dictionary)

Background / references
- Confluence spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/perf-baseline-dashboards-spec.json
- Perf regression policy: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/perf-regression-policy-and-thresholds.json
- Run manifest ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0172-benchmark-metrics-and-run-manifest-format.json
- SLO alignment: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-alignment-for-perf-baselines.json

Design requirements (v1)
1) Baseline overview dashboard (Audience: runtime leads, exec sponsors)
- “Baseline anchor” selector (runtime tag/build + baseline_freeze_date)
- Key tables:
  - TTFT p50/p95/p99 by (model, workload, region, GPU)
  - TPOT p50/p95/p99 by (model, workload, region, GPU)
  - Throughput tokens/s (and req/s for embeddings) by (model, workload, region, GPU)
- Variance panel: coefficient of variation / run-to-run stdev over last N runs (to quickly detect noisy configs)
- “Top regressions vs baseline” (read-only when thresholding is enabled; for now show delta vs baseline reference run)

2) Runtime deep-dive dashboard (Audience: runtime engineers)
- Breakdown panels using scheduler + kernel instrumentation:
  - queue_wait_ms percentiles
  - batch_assembly_ms percentiles
  - batch_size histogram (prefill vs decode if available)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate (workload-dependent; for warm runs)
  - gpu_utilization, sm_occupancy proxy, memory_bw proxy (as available from exporter)
  - kernel_family_selected (top-k) + fallback reasons (if ENG-4827 enabled)
- Drilldowns:
  - click run_id -> manifest artifact
  - click run_id -> trace artifact (Nsight/OTel trace link if present)
  - click kernel panel -> kernel selection debug dump artifact

3) SRE / gating dashboard (Audience: on-call + perf-canary operators)
- Canary status by suite + environment
- “Gating-ready” view with:
  - last green run time by (suite, model, region, GPU)
  - alerting panels for missing data / stale runs
  - variance guardrail: highlight cohorts exceeding noise bounds
- Links to runbook sections (rerun workflow, known variance sources, escalation)

Data + tagging expectations
- All panels must be joinable on a stable set of tags (no free-text parsing):
  - run_id (UUID)
  - suite_version (e.g., rep-suite-v1)
  - workload_id (chat_streaming / long_prefill / tool_calling / embeddings)
  - cache_scenario (cold|warm)
  - model_id + model_family
  - region (us-east|eu-west)
  - gpu_sku (H100|A100|L40S)
  - runtime_git_sha + runtime_release_tag
  - scheduler_policy_id
  - harness_version

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard(s) exist in the shared "Perf Baselines" folder and are accessible to Engineering (runtime + SRE)
- All top-level baseline panels support templated filtering by model/region/GPU/workload
- Drill-down links work end-to-end for at least 1 representative run per workload:
  dashboard -> manifest -> trace (or “trace unavailable” with a reason) -> kernel dump (if enabled)
- Role-based dashboards are documented: which audience uses which dashboard, and where to start
- A short "How to read these dashboards" section is added to the perf suite runbook (or linked)

Implementation plan
- Align on data source (Grafana + Prometheus/Mimir for metrics; object storage/Artifacts service for manifests/traces)
- Add a small “artifact index” metric/event (run_id -> artifact URLs) if needed; otherwise link via consistent artifact path pattern
- Build dashboards iteratively:
  v0: baseline table + drilldown to manifest
  v1: variance + deep-dive breakdown panels
  v1.1: SRE gating view + stale-data warnings

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: metrics schema drift during Q1; mitigate by pinning panel queries to canonical names in metrics dictionary draft and adding a “metrics presence” panel.
- Risk: drilldown URLs vary by environment; mitigate by using Grafana variables for artifact base URL and enforcing run_id-based lookup.

Open questions
- Do we standardize on a trace type for baseline runs (OTel vs Nsight), or allow multiple and pick the best available per run?
- Do we store kernel selection dumps as artifacts only, or also emit a summarized metric for dashboarding?

Owner(s)
- Primary: Sergio Costa (dashboard implementation)
- Partners: Aisha Bello (SRE dashboard requirements), Allison Grant (metrics conventions), Rina Kobayashi (harness artifact paths)

2025-12-13 (Rina Kobayashi): Harness now emits run_id consistently and uploads a manifest JSON per run. Artifact path format is stable as of benchmark-lab main @ pr-21432. I’ll follow up with the exact base path pattern once the validator lands.

2026-01-10 (Sergio Costa): +1 to artifact index metric; that will solve the drilldown pain. Let’s do it. I’ll wire dashboard links to query `perf_run_artifact` for manifest first, then trace if available.
